body.text: The emergency preparedness plan will be provided at the OL stage.
body.anchor: The emergency preparedness plan will be provided at the operating license stage

body.text: It will be developed using 10 CFR 50.160 and RG 1.242.
body.anchor: will be developed utilizing the requirements in 10 CFR 50.160

body.text: The approach is performance-based, technology-inclusive, risk-informed, and consequence-oriented.
body.anchor: a performance-based, technology-inclusive, risk-informed, and consequence-oriented emergency preparedness approach

body.text: A site-specific PRA will be used to form the plan and inform EPZ size.

body.text: RG 1.242 Appendix A was used to determine EPZ size.

body.text: The preliminary analysis supports a PEP EPZ within the EAB, meeting 10 CFR 50.33(g)(2)(i).

body.text: The NRC is the primary authority for radiological events at NRC-licensed facilities.
body.anchor: The NRC acts as the primary authority for radiological events

body.text: For incidents affecting the public, FEMA may coordinate the federal response.

body.text: Notification protocols are set with the Wyoming Office of Homeland Security, Lincoln County, and Kemmerer.

body.text: A primary ERF (on-site) and a backup ERF (off-site) will be available.

body.text: Their functions are alike and similar to a Technical Support Center and Operational Support Center.

title: Emergency Preparedness
subject: emergency preparedness
intro: The emergency plan itself comes at the operating license stage. The PSAR sets out the performance-based approach, who is in charge, and what facilities will exist.

objectives.text: State the regulatory basis of the emergency preparedness approach.
Describe the Plume Exposure Pathway Emergency Planning Zone basis.
Identify who leads the emergency response.
Identify the roles of federal, state, and local agencies.
Describe on-site protective measures and protective actions.
Describe the emergency response facilities and communications.
